question: Which device is used to identify the presence of electric charge on an object?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Electroscope**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **electroscope** is a scientific instrument used to detect the presence of electric charge on an object.
 
• It works on the principle of electrostatic induction or conduction.
 
• The most common type of electroscope consists of a metal rod with thin metal leaves (usually gold or aluminum) at the bottom.
 
• When a charged object touches the metal rod, the leaves repel each other, indicating the presence of a charge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohmmeter**

 
 
• An ohmmeter is an instrument used to measure electrical resistance in ohms.
 
• It is commonly used to check the continuity of electrical circuits and measure the resistance of electrical components.
 
 
 
• **Multimeter**
 
 
• A multimeter is a versatile instrument that can measure voltage, current, and resistance.
 
• It combines the functions of an ammeter, voltmeter, and ohmmeter.
 
• It is widely used in electrical and electronic testing and troubleshooting.
 
 
 
• **Ampere Meter**
 
 
• An ampere meter, or ammeter, is an instrument used to measure electric current in a circuit.
 
• It measures current in amperes (A) and is connected in series with the circuit being tested.
